questions.question: Distinguish the members of the budget family and set the zero-based method against incremental budgeting.
questions.expected_answer: The cash budget forecasts money in, money out and the surviving balance month by month — the survival question. The capital budget schedules long-life asset purchases with their amounts, timing and funding, handing the cash budget its landing dates. Medium-term budgets plan one to three years out (range, staffing); long-term budgets carry the strategy further in broader strokes. Zero-based budgeting starts every line at nothing and demands fresh justification — what does it buy now, what breaks without it — while incremental budgeting copies last year plus a percentage and so carries dead costs forever.

questions.question: Build Lerato's three-month cash budget and state the two cash-only rules it obeys.
questions.expected_answer: Receipts each month: cash sales R21 000 plus collection of the previous month's credit sales R9 000 (30% of R30 000) = R30 000. Payments: timber and materials R18 000, wages R4 500, rent R2 500 = R25 000; plus the wood lathe R9 000 in November. October: surplus R5 000, opening R3 000, closing R8 000. November: deficit R4 000 (5 000 − 9 000), closing R4 000. December: surplus R5 000, closing R9 000. Cash-only rules: credit sales enter at COLLECTION, not at sale; depreciation never appears, because no rand leaves — the cash budget records only actual money movements.

questions.question: Read the quarter for its three decisions or lessons.
questions.expected_answer: Timing: the R9 000 lathe was deliberately placed in November where the balances could carry the dip to R4 000 — seen in advance it is manageable; bought on impulse in a lean month it could have emptied the account, and a projected negative would prompt delaying the purchase or arranging an overdraft in advance. The lag: 30% of each month's earning arrives a month late, so growth months feel tight — profit and cash run on different calendars. Control: when actual figures arrive, each variance against budget (materials above, sales below) becomes a specific investigation, catching problems while they are still small.
